author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: this is a workspace-wide architectural decision, not a per-crate fix.

The bead body explicitly flags this: 'A workspace-wide policy decision on map ordering is the durable fix; this finding is the minimum-scope fix for the field this diff touched.'

The minimum-scope fix (switch this one field to BTreeMap) is a poor choice on its own because:
1. It introduces NEW intra-workspace inconsistency: BTreeMap<String, PatchObject> for ContactCard.localizations vs HashMap<Id, bool> for ContactCard.address_book_ids in the same struct.
2. The same regression exists in jmap-tasks-types::Task::localizations (the canonical that contacts-types mirrors) and jmap-calendars-types::CalendarEvent::localizations. Per workspace canonical-template rules, the canonical changes first, then propagation — meaning this fix has to touch all 3 type crates minimum.
3. The broader pattern (HashMap throughout for wire-format maps) is in 40+ sites across 14+ crates including Email.mailbox_ids, Email.keywords, every SetResponse field, and every */set update parameter.

Filed workspace-policy epic JMAP-pdux 'Workspace policy: wire-format map ordering for HashMap<_, _> fields' with four options laid out and a recommendation for option (b) BTreeMap everywhere.

This bead remains open as the trigger and the per-crate-impact tracking; it should be closed automatically once JMAP-pdux lands a decision and the sweep reaches contacts-types.
